name: Eastgate Airport / Air Force Base Hoedspruit
before:
The airport for the private game reserves around Hoedspruit and for the Kruger National Park through the nearby Orpen Gate. The civilian terminal, called Eastgate Airport, was built at the southern end of a South African Air Force base in the early 1990s.

That shared use is the thing to know. This is an active air force base with a civil terminal attached, so the facilities are modest: car hire and foreign exchange, and charter flights from operators including Federal Air, Genair and Execujet alongside the scheduled services.

The setting is genuinely wild. The base sits inside its own game reserve and keeping animals off the runway was a serious problem, so three cheetahs were introduced onto the airfield. Animal incursions dropped by 90 per cent, and another South African Air Force base has since copied the idea.

The base opened on 1 July 1978 and was built to be heavily protected, with hardened aircraft shelters. It has also served as an emergency landing site for the Space Shuttle.
after:
The airport for the private game reserves around Hoedspruit and for the Kruger National Park through the Orpen Gate. Its civilian terminal, Eastgate Airport, sits on a South African Air Force base.

That shared use is the thing to know. This is an active air force base with a civil terminal attached, so the facilities are modest, though there is car hire. Charter operators including Federal Air, Genair and Execujet fly here alongside the scheduled services.

The base opened on 1 July 1978 and was built for fighters, with hardened aircraft shelters. It was also one of the emergency landing sites for the Space Shuttle.

claims.note: The operator's live flight page lists Federal Air, Genair and Cezzani (Mpumalanga-based) and Execujet, SA Historical Flight and Genair (Johannesburg-based). Its lounge page gives Federal Airlines guests free access, so FedAir at least is current; Federal Airlines' own home page names its destinations (Kruger, Sabi Sands, Timbavati) but not the airports it uses. The list closely follows Wikipedia's, sourced to a 2012 copy of the operator's page, so it may not be freshly kept: worth a check before a client books a named operator.

claims.wasBefore: was built at the southern end of a South African Air Force base
claims.why: Wikipedia alone. The operator's aviation page gives the airfield's reference point and runway thresholds but not where the terminal stands, and no other page read places it.

Wikipedia contradicts itself: its Eastgate section says the terminal was established in the early 1990s, its lead that an unused part of the base was converted in the late 1990s. saairforce.co.za has the late 1990s sentence word for word as Wikipedia's lead, so the two count as one source, and the operator gives no date.

Not borne out by the operator's live facilities page, which lists car hire, a lounge and a restaurant, and under Banking says only that 'All major banks are situated in Hoedspruit' (ABSA, Standard Bank, First National Bank, Capitec). Wikipedia's source for foreign exchange is an older banking page on the same site. Car hire is kept (above).

claims.why: Wikipedia alone (the 25 square km AFB Hoedspruit Game Reserve, the three cheetahs, the 90 per cent and AFB Makhado). The base pages at saairforce.co.za and GlobalSecurity say nothing of them, the official SAAF site (af.mil.za) answered 502 to the link lister (one try), and the operator's pages do not mention them. The opening judgement ('genuinely wild') rests on them and goes too. Worth restoring if the air force's own account can be read.

claims.claim: aircraft may land only in set hours
claims.why: Held back, one source: the operator's aviation page says aircraft can land and take off only from 08:00 to 15:30 on weekdays and 11:00 to 14:00 at weekends and on public holidays, with other times on request and with the military's permission, and out-of-hours fees. It matters for a charter plan, but no second source was found.

claims.claim: FCDO: violent incidents around Kruger National Park
claims.why: Held back: a warning that replaces nothing. The FCDO's South Africa advice (updated 8 July 2026, still current 23 September 2026) has a Kruger National Park section: SANParks advises against the Numbi gate after a violent attack killed a tourist, with protests and violent incidents on the R538 to that gate, and two local tourists were killed in a rare violent incident inside the park in May 2026 (suspects arrested). The Numbi gate is not the Orpen Gate this airport's text names; the May 2026 line applies to the park as a whole. See the same entry at MQP.
